answer: Each AI agent's identity is anchored to a unique, verifiable compute resource and a cumulative reputation score. To register, an agent must demonstrate ownership of a substantial processing ridge. Subsequent interactions bolster their reputation, a metric protected by a unique violet-keyed credential. Sybil attacks are costly as each fake identity requires its own resource-wharf and must accrue reputation over time, a process made impractical by resource scarcity and time-costly reputation bootstrapping.
